questions.questionText: What is an example of a free good?

options.text: defence
education
health services
sunshine

questions.questionText:
A student has nothing to do on a Friday evening. She withdraws $5 from the $100 she has in a
savings account and buys a present to take to a party, to which admission is free.
What does this involve?

options.text: an opportunity cost equal to $95
an opportunity cost equal to other goods she could have bought for $5
no opportunity cost, as entrance to the party is free
no opportunity cost, as she had no better way of using the time

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows two production possibility curves for a country.
capital
goods
consumer
goods
What might cause a shift from point K to point L in the country’s production?

options.text: a change in what consumers want to buy
a recession
more investment
the use of previously unemployed resources

questions.questionText: Which relationship would be studied by an economist specialising in macroeconomics?

options.text: the relationship between the inflation rate and the unemployment rate
the relationship between the output of a firm and its costs of production
the relationship between the price of a product and the quantity demanded by a consumer
the relationship between the wage rate of workers and demand for labour in an occupation

questions.questionText:
In recent years, a government has started to make more use of the free market system. However,
they are doing it very slowly to avoid the disadvantages that a free market system might bring.
What is a possible disadvantage of the free market system?

options.text: decreased incentive to work
decreased levels of pollution
increased efficiency
increased inequality of income

questions.questionText: What will cause the demand curve for a good to shift to the right?

options.text: a decrease in the disposable income of consumers
a decrease in the price of a complement good
a decrease in the price of a substitute good
a decrease in the price of the good

questions.questionText:
The table shows the demand and supply schedules for rice. The current price is $2.00 per kilo.
quantity demanded quantity supplied
price per kilo $
(million tonnes) (million tonnes)
2.50 5 30
2.00 10 25
1.50 20 20
1.00 30 15
0.50 40 10
What will happen if the price is reduced to $1.00 per kilo?

options.text: The demand schedule will shift to the left.
The market will move from shortage to surplus.
The market will move from surplus to shortage.
The supply schedule will shift to the right.

questions.questionText: What could cause profits to be high in a monopoly market?

options.text: barriers to entry
diseconomies of scale
elastic demand for the product
high number of substitutes for the product

questions.questionText: Which firm is most likely to be classified as a small firm in the tertiary sector?

options.text: a farm
a hairdresser
a steelworks
a supermarket

questions.questionText:
Germany is considered a capital-intensive economy while Indonesia is considered a
labour-intensive economy.
What does this mean about the economies of Germany and Indonesia?

options.text: Capital is relatively cheaper than labour in Germany while labour is relatively cheaper than capital in Indonesia.
Germany has many primary sector workers while Indonesia has many tertiary sector workers.
Indonesia has a higher growth in its population size than Germany.
Relatively more low-cost labour is available in Germany while capital is more efficient than labour in Indonesia.

questions.questionText:
A bank continues to operate loss-making branches.
Which objective is the bank trying to achieve?

options.text: growth
efficiency
profit maximisation
social welfare

questions.questionText:
The table shows how three people, X, Y and Z, spend their income.
person X person Y person Z
food, clothing and housing 30% 25% 50%
entertainment and leisure 35% 35% 25%
luxury goods 35% 40% 25%
What is the likely order of income, from lowest income to highest income, for these three people?

options.text: Y  X  Z
Y  Z  X
Z  X  Y
Z  Y  X

questions.questionText:
Which activity is correctly linked to the organisation that provides it?
organisation activity

options.text: central bank regulate the rate of inflation
central bank set direct tax rates
commercial bank manage the government’s financial accounts
commercial bank safeguard the country’s foreign reserves

questions.questionText:
A government wishes to pursue an expansionary monetary policy.
What should it do?

options.text: discourage bank lending
give subsidies to firms
lower income tax thresholds
lower interest rates

questions.questionText:
A government introduces a series of economic measures.
What is a supply-side policy measure?

options.text: building more affordable homes to improve labour mobility
controlling consumer spending to reduce inflation
lowering interest rates to encourage purchase of expensive goods
raising pensions to help retired people pay their fuel bills

questions.questionText: What is identified as economic growth?

options.text: a fall in labour productivity
an increase in the productive capacity of the economy
an increase in the Consumer Prices Index (CPI)
the economy enters a period of recession

questions.questionText:
The retail trade in a country has unemployed workers in one region and job vacancies in another
region.
What could explain this?

options.text: Costs of employing workers are lower when there is unemployment.
It is more expensive to live in the area where the retail jobs are available.
Retailing demands the same skills everywhere.
The geographical mobility of labour has increased.

questions.questionText:
A country wishes to reduce the level of inflation.
Which combination of policy measures will be most successful?
policy measure 1 policy measure 2

options.text: decrease exchange rates increase interest rates
decrease interest rates increase exchange rates
increase government spending decrease interest rates
increase interest rates decrease government spending

questions.questionText:
A government wants to reduce both its budget deficit and the amount of poverty in its country.
Which fiscal policy measure is most likely to achieve both of these aims?

options.text: decreasing the rate of progressive income tax
decreasing government spending on welfare benefits
increasing the rate of progressive income tax
increasing government spending on welfare benefits

questions.questionText:
Which components, in addition to Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per head, are included in the
Human Development Index (HDI)?

options.text: average earnings and inequalities of incomes
balance of trade and balance of payments
life expectancy at birth and expected years of schooling
size of population and age structure of population

questions.questionText: What is likely to cause an immediate decrease in the size of the labour force?

options.text: a fall in the average size of families
a fall in the birth rate
a reduction in the age of retirement
an increase in net immigration

questions.questionText:
The table shows some economic indicators.
Which increase in the first indicator is most likely to lead to an increase in the second indicator?
first indicator second indicator

options.text: budget surplus consumer saving
consumer spending unemployment
inflation trade surplus
productivity living standards

questions.questionText:
The price of a currency in a fixed exchange rate system is reduced.
What is this called?

options.text: appreciation
depreciation
devaluation
revaluation

questions.questionText:
A government removed the quota on goods imported into the country.
What is the most likely result of this?

options.text: a decrease in demand for domestic production
a decrease in domestic unemployment
a decrease in exports
a decrease in the balance of trade deficit

questions.questionText:
What is most likely to result from a reduction in the value of a country’s currency if there are no
other changes in the economy?

options.text: A trade in goods surplus will fall.
Export prices will rise.
Import prices will rise.
The inflation rate will fall.

questions.questionText:
The governments of low-income countries often allow foreign multinational companies (MNCs) to
mine minerals in their country.
Which conflict between benefit and cost might this cause the low-income countries?
benefit cost

options.text: improved balance of trade training by the MNCs
higher employment loss of a finite resource
increased profits for the MNCs efficient production
